items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to the registration of vendors of electronic cigarettes
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S2542

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to the registration
of vendors of electronic cigarettes

 PURPOSE :

To ensure all sellers of electronic cigarettes are registered and
subject to compliance checks

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one adds a new Public Health Law § 1399-dd-1 to any person
selling or offering for sale electronic cigarettes that is not
registered with the Department of Taxation and Finance to sell tobacco
products, to register with the Department of Health. The Commissioner
shall adopt regulations to establish the registry and ensure
compliance.

Section two provides the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

In 2012, the state banned the sale of electronic cigarettes to minors
under the age of 18. Despite enactment of this ban to minors in New
York and a number of other states, the CDC reports the use of
electronic cigarettes among middle school and high school students has
more than double from 2011 to 2012. The health effects of electronic
cigarettes remain unknown, and while the FDA recently issued proposed
regulations on electronic cigarettes, which includes a nationwide ban
of the sale to minors, electronic cigarettes remain unregulated. Since
they are unregulated, electronic cigarettes packages are not required
to include health warnings and they can contain flavored electronic
nicotine which can often entice minors.

Although banned to minors in this state for several years, enforcement
of this provision has been problematic. Chapter 448 of 2012 included
electronic cigarettes in the Public Health Law provisions banning sale
to minors, but did not include electronic cigarettes under the
definition of a "tobacco product" under the Tax Law. Thus, retailer's
that sell electronic cigarettes do not need a tobacco registration
from the Department of Taxation and Finance. As a result, electronic
cigarettes can be sold in stores that do not sell traditional tobacco
products. Since these retailers are not registered, there is no way
for the Department of Health's Enforcement Unit to know they are
selling electronic cigarettes and to conduct compliance checks to
ensure they are not selling to minors. By requiring retailers that are
not registered with the Department of Tax and Finance to register with
the Department of Health, this legislation will ensure the Department
of Health is aware of all retailers selling electronic cigarettes and
can then conduct compliance checks to ensure adherence to existing
law.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016: 5.6003 - Veto # 275
2015: S.6003 - Passed Senate, died in Assembly
2014: S.7139 - Passed Senate, died in Assembly

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Effective the first day of the month commencing after the 180th day
after enactment; provided addition, amendment and/or repeal of any
rule or regulation necessary for implementation is effective
immediately.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the tax law, in relation to the registration of vendors of electronic cigarettes
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S2542A

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the tax law, in relation to the
registration of vendors of electronic cigarettes

 PURPOSE :

To ensure all sellers of electronic cigarettes are registered and
subject to compliance checks

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one adds a new Article 20-C to the Tax Law, requiring any
person selling or offering for sale electronic cigarettes or liquid
nicotine, who that is not registered with the Department of Taxation
and Finance to sell tobacco products, to register under this section.
The Commissioner shall adopt regulations to establish the registration
requirement and ensure compliance.

Section two provides the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

In 2012, the state banned the sale of electronic cigarettes to minors
under the age of 18. Despite enactment of this ban to minors in New
York and a number of other states, the CDC reports the use of
electronic cigarettes among middle school and high school students has
more than doubled from 2011 to 2012. The health effects of electronic
cigarettes remain unknown, and while the FDA recently issued proposed
regulations on electronic cigarettes, which includes a nationwide ban
of the sale to minors, electronic cigarettes remain unregulated. Since
they are unregulated, electronic cigarette packages are not required
to include health warnings and they can contain flavored electronic
nicotine, which can often entice minors.

Although banned to minors in this state for several years, enforcement
of this provision has been problematic. Chapter 448 of 2012 included
electronic cigarettes in the Public Health Law provisions banning sale
to minors. Chapter 542 of 2014 expressly included liquid nicotine in
the ban to minors. Since these changes did not add electronic
cigarettes or liquid nicotine to the definition of a "tobacco product"
under the Tax Law, retailer's that sell only these products and not
traditional tobacco products do not need a tobacco registration from
the Department of Taxation and Finance. As a result, when electronic
cigarettes are sold in stores that do not sell traditional tobacco
products, these retailers are not registered and there is no way for
the Department of Health's Enforcement Unit to know they are selling
electronic cigarettes and to conduct compliance checks to ensure they
are not selling to minors. By requiring retailers that are not
registered under Article 20, to register under this new article the
bill ensures that State and localities can conduct compliance checks
to confirm adherence to existing law.

This bill also seeks to address the point raised by the Governor's
Veto message in 2016, claiming the bill would create a significant
burden on the Department of Health. Given the Department of Tax and
Finance already registers tobacco retailers, simply adding these
retailers pursuant to regulations established by the Department,
should not be an onerous new burden.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016: S.6003 - Veto # 275
2015: S.6003 - Passed Senate, died in Assembly
2014: S.7139 - Passed Senate, died in Assembly

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

 None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Effective the first day of the month commencing after the 180th day
after enactment; provided addition, amendment and/or repeal of any
rule or regulation necessary for implementation is effective
immediately.

summary: Requires retailers of electronic cigarettes, or liquid nicotine, not otherwise registered with the department of taxation and finance to sell tobacco products, to register with such department.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 186
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 2542-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the tax law, in relation to the registration of
      vendors of electronic cigarettes"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  Any retailer that sells  "tobacco  products"  in  New  York  State  is
required  to  register with the Department of Taxation and Finance. This
bill would require any retailer selling electronic cigarettes or  liquid
nicotine  to  also  register  with  the  Department, but for the reasons
outlined below, this bill cannot be implemented as drafted.
 
  This bill seeks to increase enforcement, and thereby limit  a  minor's
ability  to  purchase  e-cigarettes.  As  drafted,  however, it will not
accomplish this goal. This is because only  tobacco  products,  and  not
electronic  cigarettes  or  liquid nicotine, are subject to State taxes.
Until the definition of "tobacco product" is modified to  include  e-ci-
garettes  and liquid nicotine products, the Department has no meaningful
authority to enforce the bill's registration requirements.
 
  I fully support the intent of this  bill,  as  there  are  significant
public  health  risks associated with the use of e-cigarettes and liquid
nicotine products. In 2012, I signed legislation  banning  the  sale  of
e-cigarettes  and liquid nicotine to minors. Earlier this year, I signed
legislation banning the use of e-cigarettes on all  public  and  private
school grounds in New York State, as well as legislation adding e-cigar-
ettes  to the Clean Indoor Air Act, which bans their use everywhere that
smoking tobacco products is prohibited.
 
  While I am constrained to veto this bill, I would support  legislation
that  amends the definition of "tobacco product" to include e-cigarettes
and liquid nicotine products. I am directing the Department to work with
the sponsors and interested stakeholders to collaborate  on  legislation
that would address this concern and enhance the Department's enforcement
ability to crack down on retailers that sell these products.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
